sources.entry: django-mongodb-backend - Official MongoDB database backend for Django.

summary.one_liner: Official MongoDB database backend for Django that uses PyMongo to connect Django projects to MongoDB.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Django database engine named django_mongodb_backend that connects Django to MongoDB through PyMongo. Install a version matching your Django release (for example 6.1.* for Django 6.1.x). Start a new project from a MongoDB-provided project template, then point the DATABASES setting at a MongoDB connection string and database name. The README says a runserver check confirms the project is configured. Bugs and feature requests go to a JIRA project rather than GitHub issues. The README's links to documentation and support channels are missing from the text, so the docs locations are not stated here.
use_cases: Use MongoDB as the database for a Django web app
Start a new Django project wired to MongoDB
Connect Django models and ORM to a MongoDB cluster
Deploy a Django project against a hosted MongoDB Atlas cluster
how_to_run: django-admin startproject example --template <project template URL for your Django version>
Set DATABASES in example/settings.py with ENGINE 'django_mongodb_backend', HOST (connection string) and NAME
notable: Ships a project template for starting new Django projects
Works through Django's standard DATABASES configuration
caveats: Version must match your Django release, so you pick the package version by Django version
The README gives no details on supported features or unsupported ORM parts
Bug reports go through a JIRA project rather than GitHub issues
